_comment_history: 2026-09-25 Jax ruling: `public`'s original two commits (built before this manifest/pipeline existed) carried un-sanitized content and had to disappear from reachable history entirely -- not just get overwritten in a new commit's working tree. Every commitOntoPublic() call is therefore a single parentless (orphan) commit; `public`'s history is always exactly 1 commit deep, never a chain. Idempotency is unaffected -- it was already tree-hash-only, never parent-based (see commitOntoPublic's IDEMPOTENT check). Overridable per-invocation via the --orphan CLI flag, but this field is the standing default so an ordinary `node scripts/publish-public.cjs` run (no flags) still rebuilds an orphan commit, not a chain.

addFiles._comment: Present ONLY in 592c4c3 (public), absent from pre-cut-release -- pmm-isolation-gate.cjs's open-core cut extracted two pure Win32 filename-safety helpers out of the excluded pmm-core.cjs into this new leaf file so the gate stays self-contained.

overlays._comment: Full-content replace. Used where the private->public difference is a hand-curated narrative (README) or a dense, coupled data-file edit (guard-canary.sh's roster/EXPECTED arithmetic; isolation-gate-contract.json's allow_prod roster remap + 3 report_only downgrades + mutation-set trim) that is safer to snapshot than to re-derive mechanically. TRADEOFF (see report): these 4 files will need a manual overlay refresh whenever their private source gains new content for KEPT (non-excluded) guards -- the script does not auto-detect staleness.

replacements: _comment: each {file, findFile, replaceFile} pair does an exact, literal, whole-substring find/replace of findFile's content with replaceFile's content inside the exported copy of `file`. required=true (default) fails the export loudly if findFile's exact text is not found -- this is the forcing function that catches upstream drift instead of silently missing it.

sanitize._comment: Defense-in-depth regex scrub applied to every exported text file (not just the ones covered by replacements/overlays above), driven dynamically from the running machine's os.userInfo().username / os.hostname() -- never a hardcoded literal in this manifest or the script, so it stays correct if run from a different machine.

rules.description: the real OS username as a bare word (e.g. inside a JS string literal or comment) -> <user>

2026-09-25 Jax ruling -- ANY occurrence of the real personal-project directory name 'axervice-booking' (not just inside a real absolute path -- also test-fixture repo= values, comments, etc.) -> 'example-project'. Supersedes and replaces the old narrower 'desktop-axervice-booking-real-path' rule (username-redaction there is already covered by home-username-path above; this rule now handles the project-name half unconditionally). KNOWN INTENTIONAL divergence from today's origin/main (592c4c3), which still ships the OLD narrow-scoped behavior (byte-identical test fixture text in guards/pmm-trigger-recall.sh) -- see knownDivergencesFromCurrentOriginMain below. The private source fixtures themselves were also renamed to 'example-project' directly (guards/pmm-trigger-recall.cjs/.sh, guards/fixtures/v3/trigger-write-gate-probe.cjs), so this rule is now defense-in-depth, not the primary mechanism.

2026-09-25 Jax ruling -- the maintainer's bare first name 'Jax' (word-boundary match, so it never touches an already-mapped compound like a 'JaxStuuu'-style hostname, which the dynamic hostname rule above already handles) -> 'the maintainer'. Deliberately a hardcoded literal, unlike every other rule here -- 'Jax' is a personal name embedded in prose/comments across the tree, not derivable from any os.userInfo()/os.hostname() API the way the dynamic rules are.
